benefits: Reveals the hidden story of a photo: camera, lens settings, date, and sometimes GPS location.
Helps photographers learn — compare your settings against shots you admire.
Privacy check: see exactly what personal data your photos carry before you share them.
No EXIF library needed — the parser is hand-written, runs fully offline, and never uploads.

faqs.a: EXIF (Exchangeable Image File Format) is metadata cameras embed in JPEG files: make, model, exposure settings, date, and sometimes GPS coordinates. It lives in the file's APP1 segment and is invisible in normal viewing.

GPS tags are optional and most cameras and phones record them only if location services are enabled for the camera. Screenshots, downloads, and social-media uploads almost always have GPS stripped. Absent GPS here usually means it was never recorded or was removed.
faqs.q: Why is there no GPS data in my photo?

faqs.a: This viewer parses JPEG EXIF segments with a hand-written TIFF reader. It reads camera, exposure, and GPS tags. PNG, GIF, and WebP files show file information only, since they rarely carry EXIF.
Yes — every photo you view is read in your browser's memory and parsed locally. Nothing is sent to any server, which matters because EXIF can contain your home's GPS coordinates.
Use the Crop Image tool on this site: drawing to a canvas and re-exporting strips EXIF metadata. Alternatively, most phones have a 'remove location' option when sharing photos.
faqs.q: How do I remove EXIF data before sharing?

faqs.a: Orientation tells viewers how to rotate the photo for correct display (1 = normal, 6 = rotate 90° clockwise, and so on). Phones set this instead of rotating pixels when you hold the phone sideways.
faqs.q: What does the orientation value mean?

exif-viewer.formula:
Exposure time = numerator / denominator seconds
F-number = numerator / denominator
Focal length = numerator / denominator mm
GPS decimal = degrees + minutes/60 + seconds/3600 (negative for S/W)
Example: 28° 36' 50" N = 28 + 36/60 + 50/3600 = 28.613889°
howTo: Choose a photo from your device (up to 20 MB) — JPEG files carry the most metadata.
The file details (name, size, type, dimensions, megapixels) appear instantly.
If the photo contains EXIF data, the camera, exposure, and GPS rows appear below.
Check GPS coordinates carefully before sharing the photo anywhere.
Press New image to clear everything and inspect another file.
keyFacts: Reads EXIF metadata from JPEG files with a hand-written TIFF/EXIF parser — no libraries, no uploads.
Extracts camera make and model, software, orientation, and capture dates.
Extracts exposure settings: shutter speed, aperture (f-number), ISO, and focal length.
Extracts GPS coordinates and converts them to decimal degrees when present.
Always shows file basics: name, size, MIME type, dimensions, and megapixels.
Files without EXIF (PNG, screenshots, stripped photos) show file info plus an honest notice.

limitations: EXIF is parsed from JPEG files only; PNG, GIF, and WebP show file information without camera tags.
HEIC and RAW formats are not supported — browsers cannot decode their metadata here.
Only common tags are shown; maker notes and proprietary fields are skipped.
Values are read as stored — incorrect camera clocks produce incorrect dates.

exif-viewer.workedExample:
You inspect a JPEG from a phone camera.
EXIF stores ExposureTime as the rational 1/250 and FNumber as 28/10.
The viewer shows shutter speed 1/250 s and aperture f/2.8.
GPSLatitude stores 28° 36' 50" N, shown as 28.613889° N — check this before sharing the photo.
